How teams use it

From an incident to a proven fix

A pick fails, a shift goes badly, a new gripper behaves differently. Daedro keeps that evidence and turns it into a better robot, instead of losing it in logs and chat threads.

  1. 01

    Capture

    Import the recording your cell already keeps. Daedro finds the moment that matters.

  2. 02

    Make it a case

    The clip, robot state, gripper, software version and part, kept together.

  3. 03

    Reproduce

    Check whether simulation recreates the incident, at the recorded conditions and nearby.

  4. 04

    Try a fix

    Run the current and proposed behaviour against the case: what it resolves, what it doesn't, what it breaks.

  5. 05

    Verify everywhere

    Get a verdict for every cell and hardware setup before rollout, including where only a hardware test will do.

  6. 06

    Keep what you learned

    Log hardware trials and real outcomes. Every case becomes a test that guards future changes.

Example case

A dropped bracket, traced to one setting

A faster pick cycle started dropping heavy brackets at one cell. The case reproduced the drop, tested a fix, and showed the speed-up was fine. The softer grip was the problem.

What happened · 3.4s

The part was lifted to 17 cm, then fell 24 cm from the target.

fix verified (simulation)

Evidence

  1. Recording. The part was lifted to 17 cm, then fell 24 cm from the target.
  2. Reproduction. Simulation reproduced the incident at the recorded conditions (drop_in_transit). Nearby variations: 18 of 20 fail (slip_on_lift 9, drop_in_transit 7, success 2, misplaced 2).
  3. Fix test. v2.5.1.toml: the recorded incident is fixed (drop_in_transit → success). Across 21 runs: 19 resolved, 0 still failing, 0 newly broken.

Verify everywhere

Which robots can take this change?

Your robots run the same software on different hardware. Daedro tests a change on each setup and gives every one a verdict, so the person approving it sees the whole picture on one page.

Open the release record

On every pull request

Changes are checked before they merge

Both versions run the same seeded scenarios, plus every case in your library. If a change brings back a known failure, the check fails and the report lands on the pull request.

Scenario suite and environment
  • Suite: LHS, n=200, seed=2026; both versions ran the identical scenarios.
  • Declared operating envelope: friction 0.2–1.2; half_size 0.015–0.035; ik_noise 0–0.01; mass 0.05–1
  • MuJoCo 4.0.1 · Franka Panda (MuJoCo Menagerie eea4c74) · scripted pick-and-place, 3 cm success radius

⚠️ Simulation only. These results come from a MuJoCo model, not hardware. A pass here does not guarantee real-world performance or safety; a regression here is a lead to investigate, not proof of a hardware failure.

Robots at several sites, on different hardware.

Why does this cell struggle, and will this change help everywhere?

What happened on that bad shift, and did our fix work?

Is my new policy actually better than the last one?

Prototype scope

Works now

  • Cases from MCAP recordings with JSON channels (the format Daedro and Foxglove's JSON tools write): incident detection, clips, timelines
  • Reproduce incidents and test fixes in MuJoCo; Franka Panda trusted, SO-101 experimental
  • Release records per hardware setup, failure library, pull-request checks, video replays
  • Your own Python controller, including camera observations for vision policies
  • Logging hardware trials and post-rollout outcomes against each case

Not yet

  • Reading ROS 2 messages (CDR) directly from your bags
  • Building simulation from your own robot and cell models
  • Hosted runs, team accounts and dashboards
  • Automatic outcome tracking from your fleet, or any hardware validation

A recording shows what happened, not what a changed robot would have done. Passing in simulation does not guarantee real-world safety.
